title.narrative: Output 7.5. Increased capacity of constituents to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: 1) On 29th September 2020, the Parliamentary Committee on Industry, Commerce, Labor, and Consumer Welfare issued a directive addressed to the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Security, detailing the seven pre-conditions a country of destination must have in place in order for the Nepali government to lift the ban on migration of domestic workers, which had been in effect since April 2017.The seven pre-conditions include; a)destination countries should have a strong and separate law for ensuring services, conditions, and the protection of migrant domestic workers; b)a bilateral labour agreement with Nepal that ensures workers' basic rights like wages and weekly and annual leave; c) social security mechanisms that include the migrant worker; d) provisions on occupational safety and health; e) provisions on working hours and additional benefits for extra work; and f) 24-hour insurance coverage. Prior to issuing the directive, the Parliamentary Committee held a week-long consultative meeting, during which representatives from government ministries, civil society and the National Human Rights Commission were consulted. 2) The National Planning Commission (NPC) and the Ministry of Labour and Social Security (MoLESS) have developed draft indicators and a monitoring and reporting framework on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) related to migration, including labour migration. The piloting of the tool is being done in consultation with the government and social partners to see how the framework works and can be mainstreamed for reporting. This work is expected to be completed and operational by the end of 2021. Consultations with social partners together with all three tiers of government are underway. 1) With assistance from the Swiss Government and the UK, the ILO provided support to the Federal Parliamentary Committee for Industry, Commerce, Labour and Consumer Welfare in reaching an appropriate decision regarding existing prohibition on women migrant workers seeking employment as domestic workers abroad. The assistance included advisory services, dissemination of analytical reports on the subject, facilitation of preparatory meetings, and advocacy for the inclusion of a National Human Rights Commission representative on the team. The ILO, commissioned a comprehensive analysis of legal and policy frameworks governing foreign employment for women migrant workers and migrant domestic workers and published a report on "A comprehensive analysis of policies and frameworks governing foreign employment for Nepali women migrant workers and migrant domestic workers" in May 2021. The draft of the report was presented to the Parliamentary Committee for Industry, Commerce, Labour and Consumer Welfare in July 2020. ILO conducted a series of consultations with different stakeholders including trade union, parliamentarians, CSOs, private recruitment agencies and different government counterparts to ensure women's right to mobility in 2019 and 2020. The ILO partners advocated for women's right to international mobility and empowerment in Nepal for past many years through multi-stakeholder discussions, policy recommendations, research, and community level women empowerment interventions. 2) With support from the Swiss Government, the ILO provided technical assistance to the National Planning Commission (NPC), in developing tools, mechanisms and processes that would enable both organizations to monitor and report on SDG targets related to labour migration. This framework has been drafted based on the review of existing practices, overall SDGs results framework developed by the NPC, consultations with key experts and considering the new federal structure of governance.

description.narrative:
Nepal's Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced a program to repatriate migrant workers who were stranded in selected destination countries due to lockdown measures imposed in response to the Covid 19 pandemic, with priority given to pregnant women, those who had lost their jobs, those with health problems, those who had lost a family member back home, and those who had overstayed their visa. The repatriation program covered the costs of airline tickets, medical examinations, and other expenses, facilitating the return of 103,807 Nepalis, including many returning from Gulf countries and Malaysia, where Nepalis primarily go for overseas employment. 2) The Non-Resident Nepalese Associations (NRNA), the Pravasi Nepali Coordination Committee (PNCC), and the General Federation of Nepalese Trade Unions (GEFONT) enhanced their service delivery capacities and provided support for outreach activities aimed at facilitating the repatriation of 26,142 migrant workers (23,828 men and 1,822 women) from Malaysia, Saudi Arabia, and Kuwait who were impacted by COVID 19 and were in a precarious situation. The General Federation of Nepalese Trade Unions (GEFONT) assisted over 91 Nepali migrant workers in Qatar and referred 41 collective grievance cases (representing over 900 workers) to the Malaysian Trades Union Congress (MTUC) in Malaysia against employers for unpaid wages or delayed payment of wages. 1)The ILO repurposed its regular development cooperation program to address the Covid 19 pandemic crisis. With support from the Swiss government and in collaboration with Nepal embassies in selected destination countries, the Non-Resident Nepalese Association (NRNA), the Pravasi Nepali Coordination Committee (PNCC), and the General Federation of Nepalese Trade Unions (GEFONT), supported repatriation of Nepali workers affected by the COVID 19 pandemic in major destination countries (UAE, Malaysia, Kuwait, and Saudi Arabia). The types of assistance provided by the ILO partners include facilitating the repatriation of migrant workers in coordination with Nepal embassies in the respective countries, managing workplace grievance cases involving unfair dismissal and non-payment of wages, support to access justice, hosting health camps, disseminating information, and providing counselling services via telephone, social media, and in-person meetings.
Additionally, the ILO entered into partnership with GEFONT and the Pravasi Nepali (PNCC) network of migrant workers to build their capacities and enhance their outreach efforts in countries of destination to enable them to provide legal and information services to Nepali migrant workers in Jordan and Malaysia, as well as expanded counselling and referral services to address workplace violations of labor rights and to improve their access to accurate information.
